provenance.post_check: reviewer-name tokens replaced by [name] after the quote check

issues.text: The paper does not provide enough information about how it simulates vaccine development for a previously unknown pathogen (Disease X), so the evaluator is very skeptical of its repeated claim of a 66% chance of preventing a major Disease X pandemic.
issues.quote: I am very skeptical of its repeated claims that the portfolio will have a 66% chance of preventing a major 'Disease X' pandemic, because the paper does not provide enough information

issues.text: The paper is not convincing as a model of the future of vaccine development in its current form.
issues.quote: In its current form I do not find it convincing as a model of the future of vaccine development

issues.text: The number of doses per outbreak is fixed at 10 million rather than being a disease-specific variable; the evaluator argues it should vary and be informed by containment requirements (e.g., ring vaccination needs) and the probability that containment fails.
issues.quote: The doses per outbreak should be a variable, ideally one different for each disease, rather than fixed at 10 million.

issues.text: Much of the portfolio's returns are driven by Disease X vaccine sales, and the evaluator suspects it is wrong to include Disease X in the portfolio; at minimum a sensitivity analysis removing Disease X vaccines is needed.
issues.quote: Much, perhaps most, of the returns are driven by the 'Disease X' vaccine sales. The paper does not fully explain how this is modeled

issues.text: The paper never explains how and when the Disease X vaccine is developed and how it relates to the rest of the portfolio; if it is a separate program triggered after an outbreak, it should not be in the portfolio.
issues.quote: the paper never states how and when the vaccine is developed, and how it relates to the rest of the portfolio

issues.text: The Disease X modeling should use a viral-families approach, where existing vaccines in the same family ease development; the current framework does not reflect this.
issues.quote: A better modeling approach would be to use a viral families approach, as described by CSET and CHS

issues.text: The vaccine cost per dose is fixed at $20 based on very little information and is modeled with little rigor; market-based pricing (higher prices under monopoly, lower under competition) should be included.
issues.quote: In the primary specification, they assume a fixed \$20 per dose based on very little information.

issues.text: The paper gives little discussion of regulatory reforms to reduce clinical trial costs, treating trial costs as fixed rather than as a policy choice, even though the evaluator sees this as the main takeaway.
issues.quote: the paper authors have very little discussion of this, and tend to treat clinical trial costs as a law of nature rather than a policy choice.

issues.text: The 'Average Number of Infections' column in Table 1 is extraneous and misleading because it has no effect on the simulation, which always assumes 10 million doses sold.
issues.quote: The 'Average Number of Infections' column in Table 1 is extraneous and misleading, having no impact on the simulation.

issues.text: The bin size in Figure 3 is too large, so the histograms reveal very little.
issues.quote: The bin size on Figure 3 is much too large, and the histograms reveal very little.

issues.text: The model omits virus families associated with seasonal respiratory viruses (e.g., picornaviruses) that could have commercial markets and relevance to Disease X, and should include them.
issues.quote: There are many virus families that are candidates for a Disease X, such as picornaviruses, that are not associated with the Emerging Infectious Diseases described in this paper.

issues.text: The cost per clinical trial is not a variable input, and Table S1 does not show profitability under lower trial costs; the analysis should show how much cheaper trials would need to be for profitability.
issues.quote: The cost per clinical trial should be a variable input, and Table S1 should show profitability with lower trial costs.

issues.text: Table S1, which the evaluator sees as the most useful output, is buried in the supplement and is limited in its policy choices; it should be moved to the main text and expanded to include more policy options.
issues.quote: In particular, Table S1 should be promoted to the main body of the paper, discussed more, and expanded.
